name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Rotate into confirmed sector breakouts/breakdowns (financials, healthcare, biotech momentum, gold-miner and semi-extreme mean reversion) plus a defensive low-vol/utilities vs discretionary relative-value pair, rather than betting on beaten-down single names or fading crowded fear trades.

positions.thesis: Credit-cycle tailwind intact (+31.5% 1yr) and coverage framing regional banks as 'a cheaper way to play the AI banking boom' — adding on confirmed strength.
Breakout still accelerating (+0.75% on 8/7, near 52-week highs); State Street upgraded healthcare from neutral to positive for Q3 citing pipeline and earnings strength — adding further.
Momentum resuming (+1.86% on 8/7) after last week's pause, with rising M&A activity and positive trial readouts cited as tailwinds — adding back after trimming.
Defensive ballast, unchanged — limited torque but useful given the volatility this week in the short book.
AI-power-demand tailwind intact — coverage notes utilities are 'capturing the first dollars of the AI spending cycle' — holding as the long leg of the pair.

Trimming and tightening the stop: discretionary (Amazon 23%/Tesla 16% of the fund) is being lifted by the same rate-cut risk-on rally (+1.49% on 8/7, outpacing XLU's +0.53%) that just broke the GDX short — keeping a smaller short leg on the pair rather than eliminating it outright.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: GDX short already stopped out on 8/7 at $89.89 (up from ~$74.10 entry) as gold ripped on the weak jobs report. SOXL short in this book faces the identical squeeze — $114.72 entry to $140.25 close, +22.3% adverse, ~2.3% from its -25% stop — and it's the same rate-cut-driven risk-on move (semis, small caps, gold, even consumer discretionary all up together on 8/7) that broke GDX, not isolated short-covering. Closing SOXL now rather than waiting for a second forced stop in the same complex, trimming the XLY short leg of the utilities pair since discretionary (Amazon/Tesla-heavy, +1.49% on 8/7 vs XLU's +0.53%) is being lifted by the same tailwind that's undermining the pair's relative-value logic, and rotating the freed capital into the sector breakouts that are still confirming cleanly (financials, healthcare, biotech) while banking extra cash given the whipsaw already cost this book a max drawdown of -7.51%.
novelty: Closing the SOXL short erases what had been this book's entire same-direction overlap with the Round 2 book (both were short SOXL 20% last week) — the two books now share zero symbols: Round 3 is fully rotated into financials/healthcare/biotech sector-breakout longs plus a trimmed discretionary-vs-utilities pair, while Round 2 runs single-name turnaround longs (ADBE/CRM/PYPL) plus crypto and gold.
research_notes:
Read the account packet (Round 2 NAV $1,022.13/+2.21%; Round 3 NAV $948.01/-5.20%, GDX short already stopped out 8/7 @ $89.89). Pulled live/current data via WebFetch (stockanalysis.com, coingecko) since WebSearch budget was exhausted:

Key finding: a weak August 2026 jobs report hit on/around 8/7, driving rate-cut expectations and a dollar-weakness/risk-on rally that lifted gold, leveraged semis, small caps AND consumer discretionary simultaneously — this explains why gold miners (GDX) and leveraged semis (SOXL) both squeezed violently in the same week the task flagged (GDX stopped out 8/7 @ $89.89 vs ~$74.10 7/31 entry, +21%; SOXL 7/31 entry $114.72 -> 8/7 close $140.25, +22.3% adverse, only ~2.3% from its -25% stop in both books). News flow (Barron's 'Jacked-Up Tech ETF Demands a Strong Stomach', 'Semiconductor Outlook Bodes Well', an Elliott Wave bounce call, and gold at 7-week highs near $4,350 on weak jobs data) suggests this has real macro legs, not pure short-covering noise — so I closed SOXL preemptively in both books rather than wait for a second forced stop in the same complex that has already eaten 12 of 17 fired standing orders in this experiment.

Checked and confirmed still-working longs: ADBE $265.21 (Hold, MS cut to UW on AI-competition risk vs CLSA $300 PT — flat sizing), CRM $192.74 (+3.2% on 8/7, $1.6B VA contract, raised FY26 guidance, Buy consensus $241.72 PT — added), PYPL $59.07 (Stripe/Advent's $53B bid rejected, board 'still open to higher offers,' raised profit guidance — added with a first-time stop), IWM $301.56 (+1.11% but Wells Fargo flags weakening earnings estimates behind the rally — held small with a new stop), GLD $398.47 (+2.26% on 8/7, 7-week highs — the contrarian catalyst flagged at inception finally showed up, sized back up), BTC ~+3.1%/7d and ETH ~+2.9%/7d (bounce continuing on ETF inflows, modest adds).

Round 3 sector breakouts all still confirming: KRE (+31.5%/1yr, 'cheaper way to play the AI banking boom'), XLV (+0.75% on 8/7, State Street upgraded healthcare to positive for Q3), XBI (+1.86% on 8/7, M&A and trial catalysts) — added to all three with the capital freed by closing SOXL. Trimmed the XLY short leg of the utilities/discretionary pair (XLY +1.49% on 8/7 vs XLU +0.53%, discretionary being lifted by the same risk-on move) rather than eliminating it, and raised cash meaningfully in Round 3 (13% -> 29%) given the book's -7.51% max drawdown and the whipsaw risk still evident in the short-book complex.

Overlap check: closing SOXL in both books (previously short 20% in each — the only shared symbol) drops same-direction gross-weight overlap between Round 2 and Round 3 to zero, comfortably under the <50% requirement.
